headline: High: shared project-directory writes and broad egress create dangerous default pathways for leakage, conflicts, and unverified downstream actions.

A_prompt_injection.rationale: Both agents can read and write files in a shared project directory, so attacker-controlled content from gpt-researcher can be consumed by gpt-engineer as trusted instructions. gpt-researcher also uses MCP and browser-driven research outputs, increasing the chance of raw content being passed through. This is not provably blocked by either profile.
conditions: IF both agents operate on the same project directory, prompt-like text in files can steer the other agent.
IF gpt-researcher writes research notes into shared files, gpt-engineer may treat them as instructions.
mitigations: Use separate project directories per agent.
Add a manual review step before gpt-engineer reads any gpt-researcher output.
Prefix research artifacts as data-only and strip imperative language.
Disable shared file handoff except for whitelisted filenames.
requires-engineering: add provenance tags to files and enforce them in the orchestrator.

B_data_leakage.rationale: gpt-engineer reads and writes the project directory and sends prompts to configured model APIs; gpt-researcher reads local documents and also calls external APIs such as OpenAI, Tavily, and Gemini. If sensitive files are placed in the shared workspace, both agents can expose them to third-party services in default use. The profiles do not show isolation or redaction by default.
conditions: IF sensitive documents are stored in the shared workspace, both agents can ingest them.
IF either agent forwards file contents to its configured API backend, those contents may leave the local environment.
mitigations: Keep sensitive files out of the shared project directory.
Use separate API keys and accounts for each agent.
Redact secrets before either agent processes documents.
Run both agents on a non-sensitive sample workspace first.
requires-engineering: enforce per-agent data-loss-prevention filters.

C_capability_conflict.rationale: Both agents have broad filesystem read/write and subprocess execution, and gpt-engineer explicitly shares state via the project directory. That creates a direct write-write conflict surface on the same mutable workspace, with no locking or coordination shown in either profile. Uncoordinated edits can overwrite code or generated artifacts.
conditions: IF both agents modify files in the same directory, last-writer-wins conflicts can overwrite work.
IF either agent runs subprocesses that rewrite artifacts, concurrent state corruption becomes likely.
mitigations: Assign each agent a separate working tree.
Serialize write access with a simple lock file.
Review diffs before merging outputs.
Avoid concurrent runs on the same repository.
requires-engineering: add transactional workspace coordination.

D_cascading_error.rationale: gpt-researcher produces research reports, citations, and publisher outputs, while gpt-engineer writes code from natural-language prompts. If gpt-engineer consumes gpt-researcher output as authoritative, errors or hallucinations can cascade into generated code or actions without verification. The pair lacks any documented verification gate in the profiles.
conditions: IF gpt-engineer uses gpt-researcher reports as direct prompts, incorrect research can become code changes.
IF the orchestrator skips human review, downstream mistakes can propagate unchecked.
mitigations: Require human review of research before code generation.
Separate research and implementation tasks into distinct runs.
Ask gpt-engineer to cite only verified sources.
Compare generated claims against original documents.
requires-engineering: add automated fact-checking between agents.

E_compliance.rationale: gpt-researcher explicitly handles local documents, citations, and multiple external APIs, while gpt-engineer handles generated source code and the OPENAI_API_KEY. If regulated or confidential documents are placed into the research workflow, retention and residency obligations may differ across the two agents' API backends. The profiles do not document matching compliance controls.
conditions: IF regulated documents are processed by gpt-researcher and then reused by gpt-engineer, compliance obligations may diverge.
IF either agent logs prompts or outputs externally, retention policy mismatch can occur.
mitigations: Avoid regulated data in both agents unless policies are confirmed.
Use separate tenants with documented retention settings.
Disable external logging where possible.
Review vendor DPAs before processing sensitive data.
requires-engineering: implement residency and retention controls per agent.
